ops.body:
Correction and a second, distinct finding after further measurement.

**`TestRestackGTFailures` does NOT hang.** I initially read it as a second hang because it appeared in the `-race` timeout's "running tests" list. Re-run at clean HEAD (`baffb08`, no `-race`, 240s cap) it passes:

```
--- PASS: TestRestackGTFailures (109.19s)
ok  github.com/yasyf/cc-context/internal/cli  109.461s
```

It was simply the test in flight when the package alarm fired. Only `TestShipGateProbe/authenticated_outside_a_repo` genuinely hangs.

**Second problem, independent of the hang: `internal/cli` exceeds the 10m default package timeout under `-race`.** With `-skip TestShipGateProbe`, the package still panicked at `test timed out after 10m0s` with `TestRestackGTFailures` at 1m40s in. So even once the hang is fixed, `task test` stays red on this package unless one of these lands:

- the gt-lane tests get faster (109s for one test suggests real sleeps/backoff waits that could be driven by an injected clock), or
- `internal/cli` gets a longer `-timeout`, or
- the slow gt-lane tests move behind a build tag / short-mode skip.

Which of those is right is the same owner call as the hang itself, so folding it into this bug rather than filing separately. Acceptance criteria updated in spirit: `task test` completing green requires both the hang fixed *and* the package fitting its timeout.
